content.title: Ayyam al-Bid Fasts of Rabi‘ al-Thani Begin on September 25
content.subtitle: Suhoor should be taken on Thursday night
content.body:
The Ayyam al-Bid fasts of the current month of Rabi‘ al-Thani in Bangladesh will be observed on September 25, 26, and 27, corresponding to Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, respectively. This means the first fast will begin on Friday, so Suhoor should be taken on Thursday night. Those who are able are encouraged to prepare in advance and make an intention to observe these blessed voluntary fasts.

The term Ayyam al-Bid is composed of two Arabic words. Ayyam means “days,” while Bid means “bright,” “white,” or “radiant.” The 13th, 14th, and 15th days of every lunar month are known as Ayyam al-Bid. Several authentic hadiths encourage Muslims to fast on these three days, and observing these fasts was a regular Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ throughout his life.

Fasting three days of Ayyam al-Bid each month carries a tremendous virtue. It is described in the hadith as being equivalent in reward to fasting throughout the year.

So let us make the most of these blessed days. If we are able, let us observe these voluntary fasts and encourage our family members to join us as well. Fasting is an act of worship whose reward Allah Himself has promised to grant.

To learn more about the virtues of Ayyam al-Bid fasting and related rulings, visit: https://muslimsday.com/blog/আইয়ামে-বীজ-রোজার-ফজিলত/

May Allah grant us the ability to observe these voluntary fasts regularly and accept them from us. Ameen.
